sections.text: Introduction

This document outlines the 
 testing procedure P1, which must be performed yearly and 
may be subject to be changed according to directives of 
Central Chemical Laboratories.

This test method 
specifies a procedure for the determination of the kinematic viscosity,
ν, of liquid
petroleum products, both transparent and opaque, by measuring the time 
for a volume of liquid to flow under gravity through
a calibrated glass capillary viscometer. The dynamic viscosity can be 
obtained by multiplying the measured kinematic viscosity,
ν, by the density,
ρ, of the 
liquid.

Note 1: 
For the measurement of the kinematic viscosity 
and viscosity of bitumens, see also Test Method D 2170, and D2171.

The test method is intended for use with liquids 
for which the shear stress and shear rates are proportional.
Definitions

items:
Kinematic viscosity, 
 The resistance to flow of a fluid under gravity.

Dynamic 
 viscosity, The ratio between the applied shear stress and rate of shear of a 
 liquid, and it's a measure of the resistance to flow or deformation of a 
 liquid.

sections.text: Summary of Method

The time is measured in seconds for a fixed volume of liquid to flow 
under gravity through the
capillary of a calibrated viscometer under a reproducible driving head and at a closely
controlled and known temperature. The kinematic viscosity is the product of the
measured flow time and the calibration constant of the viscometer.
Safety Precautions

items:
The sample must be taken as MPIS - 
 procedure No TD-SS-003-r0.

Make sure the sample bottle is correctly 
 labeled.

Thoroughly clean and dry the accessories 
 before starting the test.

Make sure the sample bottle is free from 
 dust and dirt.

The sample must be kept away from 
 exposure to direct sunlight.

As oil sample must be free from water it 
 has to be taken under dry and clear environmental conditions.

sections.text: Environmental Recommendations

items:
Using solvents such as benzene and other 
 for cleaning the valve parts is dangerous, it will expose lunge to very 
 hazardous and carcinogenic chemicals, you have to wear your breathing mask.

Do not throw the sump oil in the sewage 
 because this oil will prevent the sewage treatment process collect it in tight 
 containers and return it back to the vendor to recycle it. Always remember 
 that "this oil is load for your wastes but it's valuable material for them".
Avoid oil spillage to the ground.

sections.text: Tools and Equipment
Apparatus

Viscometers, calibrated 
 viscometers of the glass capillary type, capable of being used to determine 
 kinematic viscosity measuring within the limits of the precision.

Viscometer 
 Holders, to enable all viscometers which have the upper meniscus 
 directly above the lower meniscus to be suspended
 vertically within 1 in all directions.

Temperature-Controlled Bath, Use a transparent liquid bath of sufficient 
 depth such, that at no time during the measurement of flow time, any portion 
 of the sample in the viscometer is less than 20 mm below the surface of the 
 bath liquid or less than 20 mm above the bottom of the bath.

Temperature-Control, It's within the range from 15 to 100C, 
 the temperature of the bath medium doesn't vary by more than
 0.02C of the selected temperature 
 over the selected temperature over the length of the viscometer, or between 
 the position of each viscometer, or at the location of the thermometer. For 
 temperatures outside this range, the deviation from the desired temperature 
 must not exceed 0.05C.

Temperature-Measuring Device, 
 It's in the range from 0 to 100C- 
 Use either calibrated liquid-in-glass thermometers of an accuracy after 
 correction of 0.02C or better, or any 
 other thermometric device of equal or better accuracy.

Timing 
 Device-Use any timing device that is capable of taking readings with a 
 discrimination of 0.1 s or better, and has an accuracy within
 0.07% of the reading when tested over 
 intervals of 200 and 900 s.

Electrical timing devices 
 may be used if the current frequency is
 controlled to an accuracy of 0.05% or better. Alternting currents as provided by some public power systems, 
 are intermittently rather than continuously controlled. When used to actuate 
 electrical timing devices, such control can cause large errors
 in kinematic viscosity flow time measurement.
Calibration and Verification

Viscometers- only calibrated viscometers shall be used, thermometers, and 
 timers.

Certified Viscosity Reference Standards, 
 These are for use as 
 confirmatory checks on the procedure in the laboratory.

If the 
 determined kinematic viscosity doesn't agree within
 0.35% of the certified value, recheck each 
 step in the procedure, including thermometer and viscometer calibration, to 
 locate the source of errors.

The most common sources of error are caused by 
 particles of dust lodged in the capillary bore and temperature measurement 
 errors.

The 
 calibration constant, C, is dependent upon the gravitational 
 acceleration at the place of calibration and this must, therefore be 
 supplied by the standardization laboratory together with the instrument 
 constant. Where the acceleration of gravity, g, differs by more that 0.1 per cent, correct the calibration constant as 
 follows:
 g2

 the subscripts 1 and 2 indicate, respectively, the standardization 
 laboratory and the testing laboratory.

Work to be 
Carried Out
Procedure for Kinematic Viscosity

Adjust and maintain the viscometer bath at the the required test temperature 
 within the limits taking account of the conditions and of the corrections 
 supplied on the certificates of calibration for the thermometers.

Held 
 the thermometers in an upright position under the same conditions of 
 immersion as when calibrated.

Select a clean, dry, calibrated viscometer 
 having a range covering the estimated kinematic viscosity ( that is, a wide 
 capillary for a very viscous liquid and a narrow capillary for a more fluid 
 liquid). The flow time shall not
 be less than 200 sec or the longer time noted in Specifications D446.

The 
 specific details of operation vary for the different types of viscometers.

Fill 
 the viscometer in the normal manner when the temperature of the test is 
 below the dew point. To ensure that moisture doesn't condense or freeze on 
 the walls of the capillary, draw the test portion into the working capillary 
 and timing bulb, place rubber stoppers into the tubes to hold the test 
 portion in place, and insert the viscometer into the bath. After insertion 
 allow the charged viscometer to reach bath temperature, and remove the 
 stoppers. When performing manual viscosity determinations, don't use those 
 viscometers which cannot be removed from the constant temperature bath for 
 charging the sample portion.

Use 
 loosely packed drying tubes affixed to the open ends of the viscometer is 
 permitted, but not required. If used, the drying tubes shall fit the design 
 of the viscometer and not restrict the flow of the sample by pressures 
 created in the instrument.

Reverse viscometers used for silicone fluids, flurocarbons, and other 
 liquids which are difficult to remove by the use of a cleaning agent, for 
 the exclusive use of those fluids except during their calibration. Subject 
 such viscometers to calibration checks at frequent intervals. The solvent 
 washing from these viscometers shall not be used for the cleaning of other 
 viscometers.

sections.text: Cleaning of Viscometer

Between successive determinations 
 of kinematic viscosity, clean the viscometer thoroughly by
 several rinsings with sample solvent, followed by the drying solvent. Dry the tube by passing a
 slow stream of filtered dry air through the viscometer for 2 min or until
 the last trace of solvent is removed.
 Periodically clean the viscometer with the cleaning solution, for several 
 hours to remove residual traces of organic
 deposits, rinse thoroughly with water, and drying solvent, and dry with filtered dry air. Inorganic deposits may be removed by hydrochloric acid
 treatment before the use of cleaning acid, particularly if the presence of barium salts are
 suspected. (Warning- It's essential that alkaline cleaning solutions 
 are not used as changes in the viscometer calibration can occur.)

Precision

Determinability (d)- The difference between succesive determinations 
 obtained by the same operator in the same laboratory using the 
 same apparatus for a series of operations leading to a single result, would 
 in the long run, in the normal and correct operation of this test method, 
 exceed the values indicated only in one case in twenty.

Base oils at 40 and 100C 
 0.0020 y 
 (0.20%)

where y 
 is the average of results being compared.

Repeatability-The 
 difference between succesive results obtained by the same operator in 
 the same laboratory using the same apparatus under constant operating 
 conditions on identical test material would, in the long run, in the normal 
 and correct operation of this test method, exceed the values indicated only 
 in one case in twenty.

Base oils at 40 and 100C 
 0.0011 x 
 (0.11%)

where x 
 is the average of results being compared.

Reproducibility- 
 The difference between two single and independent results obtained by 
 different operators working in different laboratories on 
 nominally identical test material would, in the long run, in the normal and 
 correct operation of this test method, exceed the values indicated only in 
 one case in twenty.

Base oils at 40 and 100C 
 0.0065 x 
 (0.65%)

where x 
 is the average of results being compared.
